description:
FOUND s512p (Opus, 2026-10-09), member 2's design note (worktree agent-ad4d28a21ff7f772a scratch/s512p/print2-design.md).  Hand-replaced A/B (scratch/s512p/ab-m2.log, best of 5 interleaved, load 1.8, whole-process wall on the tree core; the preload costs ~7 ms of load):
    fhprint 2 M    none 0.209  control 0.209  A1 (resolver reorder, SHIPPED) 0.189  A2 (A1 + this) 0.182
    fhsep   2 M    none 0.322  control 0.321  A1 0.307                               A2 0.299
A2 = (defun %p-writable-stream (v) (cond ((typep v 'sb-sys:fd-stream) (if (sb-impl::fd-stream-obuf v) v nil)) ((and (streamp v) (not (output-stream-p v))) nil) (t v)))
RULED s513 (Fable): FILED, not built -- an SBCL-internal slot dependency for ~3 %.  Revisit if SBCL exports a non-generic direction test, or with a per-handle direction flag PCL itself records at open (the cleaner shape: no internals, invalidated by nothing since a stream's direction never changes).


=== MEASURED (s515b): the "direction never changes" premise is FALSE -- NOT built ===
Built and probed the ruled shape as a one-entry memo of the last stream that answered OUTPUT-STREAM-P = T
(sb-ext:defglobal, eq test first).  Hand-replaced A/B fhprint: -4.2..-7.6 % whole process.  But CLOSE
changes the answer: SBCL's OUTPUT-STREAM-P is NIL for a closed fd-stream (the docstring of %p-get-stream's
caller says so too), and %p-writable-stream relies on it -- with the memo, `close $fh; print $fh "y"'
answered undef with $! = 25 (the write reached the closed stream and the guard caught a different error)
where perl and the base give $! = 9 (probe scratch/s515b/pr/closed.pl).  Adding OPEN-STREAM-P to the memo
hit restores 9 and costs the whole gain (+2.8 % vs none).  A memo invalidated at PCL's own close sites would
miss streams SBCL closes itself.  So the per-handle direction flag needs a CLOSE hook on every path that
closes a perl handle -- a design question, not a perf lever; left pending.
subject: PERF (filed, not built -- ruled s513): print's %p-writable-stream asks output-stream-p, a GRAY GENERIC on SBCL 2.6 (PCL dispatch, ~4-6 % of fhprint); an fd-stream test on sb-impl::fd-stream-obuf saves ~3 % more on top of #2771 A1, at the price of an SBCL internal slot
